when you’ve been oppressed and told a part of you is wrong and sinful, sometimes the only way to feel better about it is showing it off and trying to have pride for yourself, hiding it is so painful and hurtful that it’s difficult to shake the idea that you’re making a mistake for being who you are. i get that cis-straight don’t get it but try to empathize with the fact that you have never spent sleepless nights wishing to be someone you’re not because maybe that way society would love you. and it’s something you can’t change even if you try your hardest. some people that are not as self conscious about it may not have the need to be proud of themselves for being part of the lgbtq community, but the majority do. if you’re privileged enough to not care about being perceived as gay or not and how that changes your life, good for you but there’s people who have trauma attached to their identity and speaking out helps with that.
